headline: Computational methods resolve spatial cell identity, deconvolution, and gene regulation
label: Computational Methods For Spatial Transcriptomics
summary: Spatial and single-cell datasets now span timepoints, post-mortem disease tissue, and reference-missing cell types, demanding new computational frameworks.
synthesis: The common thread is computational inference of cell identity, spatial organization, and regulatory structure from spatial and single-cell transcriptomics. Deconvolution work includes SlotDeconv, which uses diversity-constrained prototypes with spatial refinement, and DeconX, which builds pseudo-cells from deconvolution residuals to estimate cell types absent from single-cell references in bulk data. SPIDER denoises spatial transcriptomics using annotated scRNA-seq references, and CellTypeAI applies locally hosted generative AI with retrieval augmented generation for scRNA-seq annotation. DESpace2 detects differential spatial expression across conditions, SpaTemGRN infers time-resolved, spatial-unit-specific gene regulatory networks from multi-timepoint slides, and ARCADIA integrates scRNA-seq with spatial proteomics without barcode pairing. What is new is extension to disease tissue: a Visium HD framework yields a 530k-cell Alzheimer's atlas from post-mortem human brain. The scAtlasTb framework addresses reference atlas construction with systematic QC and integration assessment.
